IS 1 9148- 1979 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

TAPE WRAPPED RECTANGULAR 

AND SQUARE COPPER WIRES WITH 

A TEMPERATURE INDEX OF 220 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
tion on 29 March 1979, after the draft finalized by the Winding Wires 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division 
Council. 

0.2 While preparing this standard^ assistance has been derived from 
Doc : 55 (Secretariat) 142 'Second Draft — Specification for particular 
types of winding wires — Tape wrapped rectangular copper wires with 
a temperature index of 220' issued by International Electrotechnical 
Commission. 

0.3 For the purpose of decidmg whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS ■ 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



!• SCOPE 

1.1 Geueral — This standard relates to tape wrapped rectangular and 
square copper conductors suitable for temperature jndex of 220. 

1.2 The tape shall be coated with a suitable adhesive { for example, 
fluorinated ethylene propylene). After wrapping the covering shall be 
heat-sealed to form a continuous and adherent sheath. 

1.3 Sizes — The requirements of this standard are applicable to conduc- 
tors having thicknesses from 80 up to and including 5"6 mm and widths 
from 2 up to and including 16 mm. A schedule of preferred sizes is given 
in IS: 6160-19711, 

*Rui« for rounding ofTnuzncrical values ( Ttiised). 
tSpccificaUon for rcdangalar conductors for electrical machines. 

3 



IB s 9148 - 1979 

\A Grades of Covering — Three grades of covering are specified: 

a) Fine (F), 

b) Medium (M), and 

c) Thick (T). 

In each catcgoryj single tape and double tape coverings are specified. 

2- TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 

2.1 Wire — The insulated material as received. 

2#2 Coadactor —The bare metal after remov^t] of the covering, 

2*3 Increase in Dimensfon due to Covering— The difference 
between the thickness over the tape covering and the thickness of the 
conductor. 

2*4 Tolerance — The permissible divergence of an actual magnitude 
from that prescribed. 

3. GENERAL TEST CONDITIONS 

3-1 Unless otherwise specified all tests shall be carried out within a 
temperature range of 15 to 35^C and a relative humidity range of 45 to 
75 percent. Before measurernents arc made^ the specimens shall be 
preconditioned under these atmospheric conditions for a time sufficient 
to allow specimens to reach stability. 

3.2 The wire to be tested shall be removed from the packaging in such a 
way that the wire should not be subjected to tension or unnecessary 
bends. 

3*5 Before each test sufficient wire shall be discarded to ensure that any 
damaged wire is not included m th^ test specimens. 

3*4 When no specific range of sizes is given for a test^ the test is appli- 
cable to all sizes. 

4. CONDUCTOR 

CI The conductor shall conform to 3 J of IS : 6160-1971*, 

5. APPUGATION OF TAPE COVERING 

5*1 General — Before covering, the conductor shall be completely free 
from surface defects like burrs, copper dust^ etc. 



*Spccific4tion for rectangular conductors for electrical machiiic*. 

4 



IS 1 914B - 1979 

5.2 Atrangement of La.yevs 

5.2.1 Either one or two layers of tape may be applied- 

5.2.2 The tape shall be wrapped on the conductor, tightly, evenly and 
free from creases or wrinkles, with the adhcsjve on the mside when one 
side coated. 

5.2.3 The tape shall be applied with an overlap of 45 to 50 percent 
and when two layers are used they shall be applied in the same direction 
and displaced by approximately 25 percent of the tape width* 

5*2*4 After wrapping, the tape shall be heat-sealed by suitable meana 
to form an adherent and continuous sheath. 

53 Increase in THmenHionn due to Covering — The increase in 
dimensions due to covering when drtermmed by the method as described 
in 5.1 of IS : 3855 ( Fart II )-1979* shall lie between the mmimum and 
maximum values given in Table 1.

5.4 Flexibility and Adherence 

5,4.1 FUxzbilitj^ ( Mandrel Winding Tsst ) — The covering shaJi show no 
opening or delaminatton when bent on the edge and on the flat around 
a mandrei having a diameter 4 times the width and thickness respectively. 

5*4.2 Adherence — A specimen of the wire, 200 to 250 mm long, ihall 
be ciampled between the grips of testing machine. The covering shall 

^Specification Tor rectangular and square enamelled copper conductors: f^^^t 11 
Methods of teats ( Jirst rwuion ). 



IS : 9148 * 1979 

be cut through circumfercntially at a point approximately half way along 
the measured length. The wire shall be stretched 15 percent for single 
covering and 10 percent for double covering at a rate of 1 to 5 mm/s. 

The distance of loss of adhesion shall be less than the conductor 
width. 

5.5 Heat Shock — The covering shall show no opening or delamination 
when prepared as described in 5.4,1 and subjected to a temperature of 
240 to 245**G for 30 minutes. 

Note — The requirements of dclaminaiion icat are under consideration 

5.6 Breakdown Voltage — The breakdown voltage test shall be carried 
out in accordance with Appendix A on five samples At least four out of 
the five samples tested shall not breakdown at voltages less than those 
given m Table 2 and the fifth sample shall not breakdown at the voltage 
Jess than 50 percent of the value specified.

APPENDIX A 

( Clause 5,6 ) 

BREAKDOWN VOLTAGE 
A-I. TEST VOLTAGE 

A^l.l The test voltage shall be alternating and of a nominal frequency 
of 50 Hz and approximately smusoidal, the peak factor being within the 

limits of V^2 ± 5 percent ( V3^ to 1*49 ). The test transformer should 
have a rating of at least 500 VA and should provide a current of 
essentially undisturbed waveform under test conditions. The rest 
transformer shall have a trip current setting of not more than 5 mA, 

A-l*2 The voltage is applied at zero and increased at a uniform rate of 
approximately 100 V per second until breakdown occurs. In the event 
of breakdown occurring in less than 5 seconds the rate of increase of 
voltage shall be reduced. Where the breakdown voltage is equal to or 
greater than 2 500 V, the rate of rise of voltage shall be 500 V per 
second, 

A-2. METHOD 

A-2.1 A specimen of wire 350 mm long shall have the tape removed at 
one end and be bent flatwise around a mandrel as shown in Fig. 1. 

The radius of the mandrel shall be: 

25 mm for wires with thicknesses up to and mcluding 2" 5 mm, and 
50 mm for wires with thicknesses over 2'5 mm- 

The test specimen shall be immersed in a metal container which 
shall be fitled, as shown in Fig. I, with nickel shot, nickelplatcd shot or 
stainless steel ball bearings not more than 2'0 mm in diameter maintained 
in a clean condition by washing it, for example, in trichloroethylene. 

A-2.2 The test voltage shall be applied between the bare conductor and 
metal shots ( which are earthed ).
